report: Reviewed the complete claim and sole implementation/test association in representation_spec.rs. The required completed-call families are direct function definitions, statically dispatched trait methods, dynamic trait-object methods, function pointers, and each of Fn/FnMut/FnOnce; receiver/coercion effects must be explicit tree nodes rather than replayed adjustments. Both associations are explicitly TODO. Their explanation defers dynamic, pointer, and callable-trait dispatch and the complete substitution/adjustment matrix; the latter retains verification of direct/static cases and receiver/coercion tree representation as prerequisites for completing this contract. Completing the missing families and adding assertions distinguishing all families and explicit receiver/coercion nodes is required before this deferral can be removed. The entire associated test types_calls_dispatch_families has only that TODO comment and no assertions; it cannot detect misclassified calls or replayable adjustments, and is not behavioral evidence. No production completeness is inferred from the historical mention of partial direct/static examples. This is justified deferred implementation and verification, not implemented status; no edits to the existing accounting are needed. Baseline comparison independently confirmed exact bytes for both historical source snapshots against the current whole-file fragment, unchanged claim and implementation metadata, and unchanged test metadata/body after accounting for the legacy embedded-source field moving into fragments. The historical rationale remains sufficient when interpreted as this explicit deferral. Source assessment used the captured initial inputs and review policy captured with review read; no additional implementation helpers were needed. Executed review start/read and byte/metadata comparisons, then review record; no behavior tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator separately reports 321 passing sage-meta tests and a passing root build; those results do not establish this deferred behavior.
